title: Oscar and the Letter
premise: In the river town of Aldenmoor, 1848, Isandro Voss works her father's type foundry alongside her brother Oscar, who keeps a secret correspondence with a fugitive printer accused of sedition. When the army requisitions the town and demands the shop's ledger — the only record proving which families hold legal claim to passage on the last evacuation barge — Isandro must forge, alter, or surrender the names. As Oscar's loyalty to the fugitive collides with Isandro's duty to their dying father, the siblings discover the ledger can save one family or expose the regime's stolen inheritances, but not both. In the end, Isandro prints a false edition that frees the town's names to the world, Oscar takes the blame and the barge berth meant for their father, and Isandro stays behind to rebuild the press in a town remade by its own testimony.
about_author: Sebastian Eriksen is the pen name of a former letterpress restorer who spent a decade cataloguing provincial printing archives across Northern Europe. Their fiction explores the quiet violence of paperwork and the people who keep, forge, and die for records.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Isandro Voss, cutting matrices in her family's foundry, catalogs the town's names into the great ledger while her brother Oscar burns a letter from a fugitive printer. POV Isandro. Beat: the comfort of routine, shadowed by the first hint of Oscar's secret.

chapters.title: Smoke from the Capital
chapters.summary: News arrives that revolution has reached the capital; refugees trickle through Aldenmoor. Oscar disappears at night, and Isandro finds type dust on his cuffs that matches no job in the shop's books. POV Isandro. Beat: unease hardening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Oscar's Correspondence
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV: he has been printing seditious pamphlets for the fugitive Anselm Riehl, hiding plates inside the foundry's lead pigs. He believes words can outrun the army. Beat: idealism and guilt, love for his sister warring with his cause.

chapters.title: The Requisition Order
chapters.summary: Colonel Brandt's troops occupy Aldenmoor and commandeer the foundry, demanding the ledger that proves each family's claim to berths on the evacuation barge. POV Isandro. Beat: history arrives at her own doorstep, as she always feared and never believed.

chapters.title: Names Are Not Paper
chapters.summary: The townsfolk crowd the shop, begging the Voss family to protect their entries. Father Voss, coughing blood, insists the ledger must stay honest. POV Isandro. Beat: the crushing weight of being trusted.

chapters.title: What Anselm Left
chapters.summary: Oscar reveals Riehl's hiding place and his request: print one final pamphlet exposing the colonel's sale of berths to wealthy loyalists. POV Oscar. Beat: the secret shared, and the first fracture between brother and sister.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Brandt visits the shop, courteous and menacing, offering the Voss family guaranteed berths in exchange for a 'corrected' ledger. POV Isandro. Beat: temptation dressed as mercy; duty begins to taste like betrayal.

chapters.title: Father's Hands
chapters.summary: A quiet chapter: Father Voss teaches Isandro the old punchcutting strokes, knowing he is dying, knowing she will have to choose. POV Isandro. Beat: inheritance as intimacy, love expressed through craft.

chapters.title: The First Forgery
chapters.summary: Isandro alters a single entry — a widow's name moved up the list — telling herself it is a test. It works. POV Isandro. Beat: the vertigo of power; justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: Riehl in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Oscar smuggles the wounded Riehl into the foundry cellar. Riehl argues the ledger must be copied and smuggled out as evidence; Isandro argues it will burn the town. POV Oscar. Beat: the cause becomes concrete, and costly.

chapters.title: The Widow's Son
chapters.summary: The altered entry saves the widow's son from conscription — but Brandt notices the discrepancy and begins auditing the ledger page by page. POV Isandro. Beat: triumph curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Berth for a Price
chapters.summary: Brandt confronts Oscar privately, offering him the last berth and immunity if he names Riehl. POV Oscar. Beat: love against duty made literal — one life bought with another's.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Nails
chapters.summary: Isandro discovers Oscar's bargain half-made and confronts him in the type room; their fight wrecks a case of sorts. POV Isandro. Beat: the siblings' bond at its lowest, both certain the other is wrong.

chapters.title: Father's Last Proof
chapters.summary: Father Voss, near death, pulls a final proof of the true ledger and presses it into Isandro's hands: 'Names outlive us only if they're true.' POV Isandro. Beat: grief and clarity arriving together.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: Brandt's officers seize the ledger and find Isandro's forgery; the widow's family is arrested as scapegoats. POV Isandro. Beat: the machinery of 'lawful' injustice grinding down the innocent.

chapters.title: Oscar's Choice
chapters.summary: Oscar refuses Brandt's bargain, forfeiting his berth, and instead gives the officers a false name for Riehl — buying time, not safety. POV Oscar. Beat: duty inverted; he chooses love and justice over survival.

chapters.title: Setting the True Edition
chapters.summary: Working through the night, Isandro and Oscar secretly reset the entire ledger as a printable edition — the town's names as testimony. POV alternating. Beat: exhaustion, purpose, the siblings reconciled in shared work.

chapters.title: The Press Runs at Midnight
chapters.summary: The true edition is printed and distributed through the town as the army prepares to burn the foundry's records. POV Isandro. Beat: terror and exhilaration; the press as weapon.

chapters.title: Brandt's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Copied pages reach a neutral consul; Brandt's berth-selling is exposed and the evacuation falls into chaos he can no longer control. POV Oscar. Beat: justice arriving sideways, imperfect and unstoppable.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: One berth remains. Father Voss, dying, orders it given to Oscar, who carries the ledger copy and takes Riehl's place in the prisoners' transfer to shield him. POV Isandro. Beat: sacrifice as inheritance; love as letting go.

chapters.title: What the Fire Spared
chapters.summary: The army burns the foundry, but the true edition is already beyond reach. Isandro buries her father, watches Oscar's barge vanish downriver, and salvages one case of type from the ashes. POV Isandro. Beat: desolation shot through with resolve.

chapters.title: A New First Line
chapters.summary: Months later, in the occupied town, Isandro sets the first line of a free press: the town's names, in full, as the opening page. A letter from Oscar arrives. POV Isandro. Beat: quiet triumph — history no longer happens to other people; she is setting it in type.
